history.notes:
Grade: PASS. All nine rubric items hold. Item 3 deviates from the plan's literal text in one way, explained under item 3. Branch refactor/refined-level-defined @a6a4f68, base 3fb310a.

Re-checked by the reviewer, not taken from the reports:
- full suite on the branch;
- both unit-test files;
- the symbolic law tier;
- break-its for rubric 8 and a new footprint-count break;
- a B7b probe on k32;
- an AST comparison of SymbolicDynamics.py.

1 Suite: PASS. The reviewer's run gave 1200 passed, 46 skipped, 5 deselected, 2 xfailed (203 s). -rxX lists exactly the two KNOWN_ISSUES entries: C3, and (series_members_share_the_P1_itinerary, k32_series) with wp B7b. There is no XPASS.

2 Pinning tests on both commits: PASS, on the test engineer's base and branch runs. The reviewer re-ran the symbolic tier on the branch: 11 passed and 36 visible set-asides. In the --runxfail message, class R#7<->R#9, member (6,7) at step 6 is identical on base and branch.

Teeth, checked by the reviewer: with base-branch chords paired in stable order (the B7b change, PartitionFamily.py:993 `if True`, on a scratch copy), the k32 series test becomes XPASS(strict). So the known issue flips exactly when B7b lands, and the law is not vacuous.

3 Diff scope: PASS, with one deviation from the literal text. The diff touches 8 files, not 7. The eighth is tests/invariants/test_law_case_sanity.py (+2/-1). The reviewer read test_every_law_runs_in_the_tier: it rejects a known issue whose case is not a law case unless the law id is in _STANDALONE_ISSUES, and it rejects any wp outside WP\d+|C\d|DEC-\d+. The author's approved verdict requires a strict-xfail known issue on k32_series that names B7b. No seven-file implementation can pass that guard, so the plan's file list contradicts the approved verdict. A revise could not fix this. The two lines are the minimum change, and the orchestrator ordered them. Flag for the author's debrief: the plan's file count was wrong, not the coder's scope.

4 No behaviour change: PASS, on the test engineer's own script, which is independent of the coder's compare.py. On 15 builds, all of these are equal: letter-free rules, refined_rules, M, M_1, iterated intervals and is_reliable. There are no new WARNINGs, and incomplete_footprints is empty on every build.

5 Tested-class counts: PASS. k10 1, inversion_two_blasts 2, heteroclinic 7. The per-step series counts are printed, 141 class-tests in total. Period 3 is covered: p3_series steps 7-9, heteroclinic and p3_16.

6 Stable-end skip has teeth: PASS, on the test engineer's run. With the skip removed, k28_series fails at steps 6-8; restored, it passes. Not re-run by the reviewer: a series build is needed and the k32 probe above already covers the series path.

7 In-splitting unit test has teeth: PASS. 7a fails with [1,0,1,0] vs [1,0,0,0]. The extra checks 7b, 7c and 7d also turn the law red, including the column-sum identity that catches a dropped token.

8 Odd-count INFO: PASS, re-run by the reviewer on a copy.
- The grep hits only logger.info (PartitionFamily.py:1044) and docstring text.
- info changed to warning: the unit test fails (1 failed, 8 passed).
- Counting the chain ends as folds (chain instead of chain[:-1] at :1036): the unit test fails.

9 SymbolicDynamics.py docstrings only: PASS. The reviewer's AST comparison with docstrings stripped returns True. No comment lines changed.

Mathematics against A.8d (lines 335-434): CORRECT.
- P1 = P ∨ f(∂P): the cuts are P's plus the crossings of the first images of the hole bridges, chain ends and interior folds.
- Chords: base branch in chain order, other branches in stable order (C19).
- An odd count is an incomplete footprint, recorded as data at INFO.
- Theorem T: every member has the same P1-level freely reduced itinerary; the strip argument is stated correctly.
- In-splitting: siblings have equal rows and the children's columns sum to the parent's. This is the Lind-Marcus in-split, a conjugacy with equal entropy.
- The laws check exactly these identities, plus the node set.

The coder's four deviations, all accepted:
(1) _empty_stretches keeps its signature, with the sibling _incomplete_footprints. Forced: monkeypatches in test_iterated_cut.py and test_iterated_partition.py, outside the plan's scope, depend on the old signature. The admission filters were measured equal on all 62 builds and steps. It follows the _unmarked_lobes pattern.
(2) T is in LAW_CASES_ONLY. Forced: assert_non_vacuous on deep runs where T tests 0 classes. T's depth coverage is the series test.
(3) Known-issue id series_members_share_the_P1_itinerary. Correct: under the layered id, law_tier.set_aside_pairs would build a law_case set-aside that xfails on KeyError('k32_series'), a sham. The series_ prefix is the existing convention. The author's intent (one honest strict xfail of T on k32 naming B7b) is kept.
(4) The eighth file: see item 3.

House-style notes. None of these moves the grade; they are for a later round or B7b:
- PartitionFamily.py:1007-1050: _incomplete_footprints repeats _empty_stretches' chain walk and consecutiveness test, so the image chains are looked up twice. Acceptable while the tests monkeypatch _empty_stretches. When B7b touches this code, fold the two together (e.g. update the tests' monkeypatches).
- tests/helpers/laws.py p1_itinerary_disagreements: `except ValueError: skipped` guards a state never seen on the corpus. It is defensive. It is documented as incomplete evidence, so it may stay.
- SymbolicDynamics.py module docstring: 'T and the in-splitting are laws on every build' overstates T, which runs on the law cases and the blast series only (LAW_CASES_ONLY). Suggested wording: 'laws on the law cases (T also on every blast series)'.
- KnownIssue text in cases.py:1355: 'R_7 <-> R_9' mixes positional ElementRef ids (R#7) with ElementNaming names (subscript = id+1, i.e. R_(0.0;8), R_(0.0;10)). Cosmetic; it copies the plan's wording.
- Size is about 430 lines against the plan's 200-250. This is not a rubric item.

What is good: docstrings are Google-style and match A.8d; the WARNING became one INFO per build with a describe() line; assertions are kept; there is no dead code; and the known issue is a real, falsifiable test for B7b.
